bounded_findings: ANA states that the lower Chilca river bifurcates into a south-west arm and a north-west arm.
ANA describes a 28.8 km proposed marginal-strip delimitation for the south arm and a separate planned field-topography effort for approximately 15 km of the north arm.
ANA reports that human activity has obstructed or interrupted the north arm in places.
forbidden_inferences: The 28.8 km marginal strip is not an event footprint.
The approximately 15 km planning length is not a verified channel geometry or routing distance.
Obstruction context does not define historical hydraulic capacity or an IRFEN threshold.
The two lower arms must not be unioned into one local activation geometry.

sources.institution: Autoridad Nacional del Agua / CENEPRED SIGRID
bounded_findings: The official record approves a 28.80 km marginal strip for Quebrada Chilca Brazo Sur.
The approved strip is described with 675 georeferenced UTM WGS84 markers: 362 on the right margin and 313 on the left margin.
forbidden_inferences: A marginal strip is not an observed-event footprint.
Marginal-strip markers do not by themselves define a drainage polygon or an activation outlet.
Regulatory delimitation does not establish historical conveyance capacity.

bounded_findings: ANA reports approval through RD 0641-2024-ANA-AAA.CF of 12.5 km of marginal-strip delimitation for the north arm of Quebrada Chilca.
ANA separately recalls the earlier 28.80 km south-arm delimitation.
forbidden_inferences: The north-arm marginal strip is not an event footprint.
The regulatory length is not a routing travel distance or hydraulic-capacity observation.
North-arm and south-arm geometries must remain distinct local units.

bounded_findings: CENEPRED describes a working group for the mouth of the Chilca river, explicitly referencing north and south channels in Pucusana.
The field visit was for prevention and risk-reduction planning upstream of the river divider.
forbidden_inferences: Pucusana is not established as a separate hydrologic basin by this source.
A prevention field visit is not an observed-event footprint.
The source does not provide an exact bifurcation, outlet or confluence coordinate for IRFEN routing.
